question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

He is one of those (a)/ sincere officers who (b)/ has always kept (c)/ the department free from corruption. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the pattern "one of + plural noun + who / that / which", the relative pronoun refers to the plural noun ("officers") and not to "one". So the verb of the relative clause must be plural, and "has always kept" must be "have always kept".

◦ Corrected sentence: He is one of those sincere officers who have always kept the department free from corruption.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "He is one of those" is a proper singular subject and verb, and "those" correctly points to a plural group.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "sincere officers who" is a proper plural noun phrase followed by a relative pronoun.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "the department free from corruption." is a proper object with the correct adjective phrase "free from".

 

NOTE

 

• He is one of the students who have topped (plural verb) but He is the only one of the students who has topped (singular verb, because "the only one" is the antecedent).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Many a young cricketer (a)/ have lost (b)/ the chance to play for the country (c)/ because of indiscipline. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Many a" is followed by a singular noun and takes a singular verb, although the meaning is plural. So "have lost" must be "has lost".

◦ Corrected sentence: Many a young cricketer has lost the chance to play for the country because of indiscipline.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Many a young cricketer" is a proper phrase, since "many a" correctly takes a singular noun.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "the chance to play for the country" is a proper noun phrase with an infinitive.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "because of indiscipline." is a proper prepositional phrase of reason.

 

NOTE

 

• Many a student has failed = Many students have failed; More than one member has protested (singular verb after "more than one + singular noun").

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

According to the report, (a)/ this is the first time (b)/ that the firm (c)/ made a profit in this sector. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After "It is / This is the first time", the clause that follows takes the present perfect tense: "the first time that + has / have + V3". So "made" must be "has made".

◦ Corrected sentence: According to the report, this is the first time that the firm has made a profit in this sector.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "According to the report," is a proper introductory phrase that names the source.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "this is the first time" is a proper present tense clause that begins the pattern.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "that the firm" is a proper conjunction followed by a singular subject.

 

NOTE

 

• This is the first time I have visited Goa; It is the third time she has failed; but in the past, It was the first time he had seen snow (past perfect).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The principal, along with (a)/ the senior teachers, are (b)/ meeting the parents today. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Words such as along with, as well as, together with, in addition to, with and no less than do not make the subject plural. The verb agrees with the first subject, "The principal" (singular). So "are" must be "is".

◦ Corrected sentence: The principal, along with the senior teachers, is meeting the parents today.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The principal, along with" is a proper singular subject followed by a linking phrase.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "meeting the parents today." is a proper participle phrase that completes the present continuous.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "are" in part (b) does not agree with the singular subject.

 

NOTE

 

• The teacher, along with the students, is; The boys, as well as their coach, were (the verb follows the first subject) but The manager and the clerks are (with "and", the subject is plural).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

As soon as you will complete (a)/ the online registration, (b)/ you will receive (c)/ the admit card by post. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a time clause beginning with as soon as, when, after, before, until, once or while, the simple present is used for a future meaning, and "will" is not used. So "will complete" must be "complete".

◦ Corrected sentence: As soon as you complete the online registration, you will receive the admit card by post.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the online registration," is a proper object noun phrase.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "you will receive" is a proper simple future in the main clause.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "the admit card by post." is a proper object with a prepositional phrase of means.

 

NOTE

 

• I will call you when I reach, We will wait until he comes, She will leave before it rains — "will" goes in the main clause only. The same holds for if and unless clauses: If it rains, we will stay at home.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

She would rather (a)/ to resign immediately (b)/ than accept (c)/ such an insulting offer. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Would rather" is followed by the base form of the verb without "to", and the verb after "than" takes the same form. So "to resign" must be "resign".

◦ Corrected sentence: She would rather resign immediately than accept such an insulting offer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "She would rather" is a proper modal expression of preference.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "than accept" correctly uses the base form, parallel to "resign".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "such an insulting offer." is proper, with the correct pattern "such + an + adjective + noun".

 

NOTE

 

• would rather + base verb — I would rather stay; would rather + subject + past tense (for another person) — I would rather you stayed; prefer + gerund + to + gerund — She prefers walking to driving.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The old beggar was laughed by (a)/ the children, (b)/ but he remained calm (c)/ and cheerful. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A verb + preposition combination keeps its preposition in the passive voice. "Laugh at" therefore becomes "was laughed at by", and "was laughed by" must be "was laughed at by".

◦ Corrected sentence: The old beggar was laughed at by the children, but he remained calm and cheerful.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the children," is a proper agent of the passive verb.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "but he remained calm" is a proper clause of contrast, with "remained" as a linking verb followed by an adjective.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "and cheerful." is a proper adjective complement, parallel to "calm".

 

NOTE

 

• The child was looked after by the nurse, The proposal was turned down, The order was carried out, He was laughed at by all — the preposition or particle stays with the verb in the passive.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

From the balcony, (a)/ we watched the children (b)/ to play cricket in the lane. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After verbs of perception (see, watch, hear, notice, feel) in the active voice, the object is followed by the base form (a complete action) or the -ing form (an action in progress), and not by "to". So "to play" must be "play" (or "playing").

◦ Corrected sentence: From the balcony, we watched the children play (or playing) cricket in the lane.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "From the balcony," is a proper introductory prepositional phrase of place.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "we watched the children" is a proper subject, verb and object in the simple past.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "to play" in part (c) is incorrect.

 

NOTE

 

• I saw him enter / entering, We heard her sing / singing (active voice) but He was seen to enter, She was heard to sing (in the passive, "to" returns).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The comedian's jokes were so funny (a)/ that the entire audience (b)/ could not help (c)/ to laugh. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "cannot help" is followed by a gerund (-ing form). So "could not help to laugh" must be "could not help laughing".

◦ Corrected sentence: The comedian's jokes were so funny that the entire audience could not help laughing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The comedian's jokes were so funny" is a proper plural subject and verb, with the "so + adjective" pattern.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "that the entire audience" is a proper result clause opener with a singular collective subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "could not help" is a proper modal phrase that is completed by a gerund.

 

NOTE

 

• cannot help laughing = cannot help but laugh = cannot but laugh; other gerund idioms — It is no use crying, be busy writing, spend time reading, feel like going.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The heavy snowfall (a)/ prevented the tourists (b)/ to reach the valley (c)/ before nightfall. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The verb "prevent" follows the pattern "prevent + object + from + gerund". So "to reach" must be "from reaching".

◦ Corrected sentence: The heavy snowfall prevented the tourists from reaching the valley before nightfall.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The heavy snowfall" is a proper singular subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "prevented the tourists" is a proper simple past verb with its object.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "before nightfall." is a proper prepositional phrase of time.

 

NOTE

 

• prevent / stop / prohibit / discourage / dissuade + object + from + -ing — stopped him from going; but allow / permit / force / compel + object + to-infinitive — allowed him to go.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

My uncle (a)/ learnt me (b)/ to ride a bicycle (c)/ when I was six years old. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Learn" means to gain knowledge oneself, while "teach" means to give knowledge to another person. The uncle gave the knowledge, so "learnt me" must be "taught me".

◦ Corrected sentence: My uncle taught me to ride a bicycle when I was six years old.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "My uncle" is a proper singular subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "to ride a bicycle" is a proper to-infinitive after "teach + object".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "when I was six years old." is a proper past clause of time.

 

NOTE

 

• teach – taught – taught (give lessons) — She taught me French; learn – learnt / learned (acquire) — I learnt French from her; the same holds for lend / borrow and bring / take.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

Unless the workers do not end (a)/ the strike, (b)/ the factory will remain closed. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Unless" already means "if … not", so the verb of an "unless"-clause must be affirmative. A negative verb creates a double negative. So "Unless … do not end" must be "Unless … end".

◦ Corrected sentence: Unless the workers end the strike, the factory will remain closed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the strike," is a proper object noun phrase.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "the factory will remain closed." is a proper simple future main clause, with "remain" as a linking verb followed by an adjective.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "do not end" in part (a) creates a double negative.

 

NOTE

 

• Unless you work hard, you will fail (= If you do not work hard, you will fail); never Unless you do not work hard. Also, lest takes "should": Work hard lest you should fail.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

In her spare time, (a)/ she enjoys reading novels, (b)/ listening to music, (c)/ and to play chess. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Items joined by "and" must be in the same grammatical form (parallel structure). "Enjoy" is followed by the gerund, and "reading" and "listening" are gerunds. So "to play chess" must be "playing chess".

◦ Corrected sentence: In her spare time, she enjoys reading novels, listening to music, and playing chess.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "In her spare time," is a proper introductory prepositional phrase.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "she enjoys reading novels," is a proper singular verb followed by a gerund object.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "listening to music," is a proper gerund with the correct preposition "to".

 

NOTE

 

• She likes reading, writing and painting (all gerunds); He wants to sing, dance and act (all infinitives) — never reading and to write.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The unexpected floods compelled the villagers leave (a)/ their homes and (b)/ move to the school (c)/ before dawn. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The verb "compel" (like force, order, advise, allow, permit, urge) follows the pattern "verb + object + to-infinitive". So "compelled the villagers leave" must be "compelled the villagers to leave".

◦ Corrected sentence: The unexpected floods compelled the villagers to leave their homes and move to the school before dawn.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "their homes and" is a proper object noun phrase followed by a conjunction.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "move to the school" is a proper base verb, parallel with "to leave" under the same "to".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "before dawn." is a proper prepositional phrase of time.

 

NOTE

 

• force / compel / order / advise / allow / permit / persuade / urge + object + to + verb — forced her to sign; but make / let + object + base verb — let him go, made her sign.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The committee has decided (a)/ that the meeting be postponed (b)/ till further notice. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is grammatically correct. After verbs of decision, request or demand (decide, propose, suggest, insist, recommend, demand), a "that"-clause may use the subjunctive (base form), so "that the meeting be postponed" is correct. The collective noun "committee", acting as one unit, takes the singular "has".

◦ Sentence as given: The committee has decided that the meeting be postponed till further notice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The committee has decided" is a proper singular collective subject with a present perfect verb.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "that the meeting be postponed" is a proper subjunctive passive clause, with the base form "be" used after "decided that".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "till further notice." is a proper adverbial phrase of time.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not over-correct: The doctor insisted that he take rest; The board demanded that the report be submitted; It is essential that every student be present — the base form is used, without "-s" or "will".

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

No sooner did the guests arrive than the lights went out.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. had the guests arrived.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A sentence beginning with "No sooner" takes the past perfect in the first clause, with inversion (the auxiliary before the subject), and the simple past after "than": "No sooner had + subject + V3 … than + V2". So "did the guests arrive" must be "had the guests arrived".

◦ Corrected sentence: No sooner had the guests arrived than the lights went out.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "the guests had arrived" — the tense is right, but the inversion required after "No sooner" is missing.

 

• Option 3: "have the guests arrived" — the present perfect does not match the simple past "went out".

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because "did the guests arrive" uses the simple past instead of the past perfect.

 

NOTE

 

• No sooner had he left than it began to rain = Hardly / Scarcely had he left when it began to rain; without inversion — He had no sooner left than it began to rain. Never No sooner … when or Hardly … than.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

The accident ___ avoided if the driver had been more careful.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. could have been.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The "if"-clause uses the past perfect ("had been"), so it describes an unreal past situation. The main clause needs "would / could / might have + V3", and in the passive it is "could have been avoided".

◦ Complete sentence: The accident could have been avoided if the driver had been more careful.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "can have been" — "can have + V3" is not used in affirmative statements; it appears only in negatives and questions, such as "cannot have been".

 

• Option 3: "could be" — this refers to the present or future, so it does not fit an unreal past condition.

 

• Option 4: "should be" — this shows a present duty or probability, so it does not fit the past condition.

 

NOTE

 

• could have + V3 (a past possibility not realised), should have + V3 (a duty not done), must have + V3 (strong deduction), cannot have + V3 (impossibility), needn't have + V3 (an unnecessary action that was done).

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

Waiting for the bus at the corner, a stone hit the boy on the head.
option_1: a stone was hitting the boy on the head
option_2: the stone hitting the boy on the head
option_3: the boy was hit on the head by a stone
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the boy was hit on the head by a stone.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A participle phrase at the beginning of a sentence must refer to the subject of the main clause. "Waiting for the bus" describes the boy, but the subject of the main clause is "a stone", which makes the sentence say that the stone was waiting (a dangling participle). The subject must be "the boy".

◦ Corrected sentence: Waiting for the bus at the corner, the boy was hit on the head by a stone.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "a stone was hitting the boy on the head" — the subject is still "a stone", so the participle still dangles.

 

• Option 2: "the stone hitting the boy on the head" — this has no finite verb and leaves the sentence incomplete.

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because the given clause makes "a stone" the one that was waiting.

 

NOTE

 

• Waiting for the bus, the boy was hit by a stone; Having finished his work, he went home (the same person does both actions) — but Having finished the work, the bell rang is wrong.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

The visitors were strictly ___ to enter the laboratory without permission.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. forbidden.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passive voice is formed with "be + third form (V3)". The verb "forbid" has the forms forbid – forbade – forbidden, so "were strictly" must be followed by "forbidden".

◦ Complete sentence: The visitors were strictly forbidden to enter the laboratory without permission.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "forbade" — this is the simple past (V2), and it cannot follow "were" in the passive.

 

• Option 3: "forbid" — this is the base form, which cannot follow "were" in the passive.

 

• Option 4: "forbidding" — this is the present participle, which does not give the passive meaning needed here.

 

NOTE

 

• forbid – forbade – forbidden, forgive – forgave – forgiven, forsake – forsook – forsaken, shake – shook – shaken, take – took – taken: the passive and the perfect tenses need V3.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

He did nothing but to complain about the food all evening.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. complain.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After "do nothing but" (also cannot but, do anything but, all he did was), the verb takes the bare infinitive (base form), without "to". So "to complain" must be "complain".

◦ Corrected sentence: He did nothing but complain about the food all evening.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "complaining" — the -ing form is not used after "do nothing but".

 

• Option 3: "complained" — the tense is already shown by "did", so the past form is wrong.

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because the to-infinitive is not used after "did nothing but".

 

NOTE

 

• do nothing but complain, cannot but admire, did all but win (bare infinitive) but had no choice but to leave (here "choice" is a noun, so "to" is used).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

Now that the deadline has passed, it is no use ___ about the delay.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. complaining.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The expressions "It is no use / no good / not worth" are followed by a gerund (-ing form). So the correct word is "complaining".

◦ Complete sentence: Now that the deadline has passed, it is no use complaining about the delay.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "to complain" — the to-infinitive is not used after "no use".

 

• Option 2: "complained" — the past form is not used after "no use".

 

• Option 4: "complain" — the base form is not used after "no use".

 

NOTE

 

• It is no use crying, It is no good waiting, There is no point in arguing, It is worth trying — the gerund follows all of these.

question: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct.
option_1: The team is consisted of eleven players.
option_2: The team comprises of eleven players.
option_3: The team composes of eleven players.
option_4: The team consists of eleven players.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The team consists of eleven players.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Option 4 is correct. The verb "consist" is intransitive, and it is followed by "of": "consists of".

◦ Correct sentence: The team consists of eleven players.

 

• Each of the other three options contains a different verb error, explained below.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "is consisted of" — "consist" is intransitive, so it cannot be used in the passive voice.

 

• Option 2: "comprises of" — "comprise" is transitive and takes its object directly: "comprises eleven players".

 

• Option 3: "composes of" — "compose" is transitive (= to make up) and is not followed by "of"; the correct passive is "is composed of".

 

NOTE

 

• consists of = is composed of = comprises (no "of"): The team consists of eleven players, The team is composed of eleven players, The team comprises eleven players.

question: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct.
option_1: I wish I have a bigger house.
option_2: I wish I will have a bigger house.
option_3: I wish I had a bigger house.
option_4: I wish I have had a bigger house.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. I wish I had a bigger house.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Option 3 is correct. "Wish" for an unreal present situation is followed by the simple past: "I wish I had". Present forms and "will" cannot follow "wish" for one's own situation.

◦ Correct sentence: I wish I had a bigger house.

 

• Each of the other three options contains a different verb error, explained below.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "I wish I have" — the present tense cannot express an unreal wish; the past form is needed.

 

• Option 2: "I wish I will have" — "will" is not used after "wish" to talk about one's own unreal situation.

 

• Option 4: "I wish I have had" — the present perfect is not used after "wish"; a past regret needs the past perfect ("had had").

 

NOTE

 

• I wish I knew (present regret), I wish I had known (past regret), I wish you would stop (annoyance about another person), If only I had more time.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

After the formal introduction, the chairman ___ to announce the results.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. proceeded.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Proceed" means to go on or continue, and "proceed to + verb" means "go on to do something". The past tense is needed after "the chairman", so the correct word is "proceeded". "Precede" means to come before.

◦ Complete sentence: After the formal introduction, the chairman proceeded to announce the results.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "preceded" — "precede" means to come before something, which does not fit "to announce".

 

• Option 2: "proceed" — this is the base form, and the past tense is needed here.

 

• Option 3: "preceding" — this is a participle and leaves the sentence without a finite verb.

 

NOTE

 

• proceed (go ahead) — proceed with the plan, proceed to the next round; precede (come before) — Summer precedes the monsoon; precedent (an earlier example), procedure (a method).

question: Select the sentence that is grammatically incorrect.
option_1: By the time we reached the station, the train had already left.
option_2: She has been working in this bank since 2019.
option_3: The minister is said to have resigned last year.
option_4: I have met the new manager yesterday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. I have met the new manager yesterday.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Option 4 is incorrect. The present perfect cannot be used with a definite past time expression such as "yesterday", "last year", "in 2019" or "two days ago". The simple past is needed, so "have met" must be "met".

◦ Corrected sentence: I met the new manager yesterday.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 is correct — the past perfect "had already left" correctly shows the earlier of two past actions.

 

• Option 2 is correct — the present perfect continuous "has been working" is properly used with "since 2019".

 

• Option 3 is correct — the perfect infinitive "to have resigned" shows an earlier event, and "last year" is a proper past time expression.

 

NOTE

 

• I met him yesterday, She left in 2019, They arrived two days ago (simple past with a definite time) but I have already met him, She has just left (present perfect with an indefinite time).
